newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM says squeezed margins dented Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: DSM says squeezed margins dented Q3 profit.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Tuesday third quarter net had been squeezed at both ends by lower prices and higher feedstock costs which narrowed margins.
The company earlier reported third quarter net profits down 56 million guilders at 178 million. Operating profits in the quarter fell 103 million guilders to 239 million guilders.
"This was mainly due to lower margins caused on the one hand by lower prices and on the other by higher feedstock costs (especially for naphtha)," DSM said in a statement.
Sales volumes had risen for almost all products, it added.
DSM said it expected the supply and demand situation for its major products to remain good over the next few months.
But it said fourth-quarter results would be influenced by higher feedstock costs, particularly for naphtha, as well as by several planned maintenance shutdowns.
"We expect that it will only be possible to pass on a part of the increase in feedstock costs via the prices of our products," the statement said.
DSM said it was maintaining its forecast 1996 would be a good year.
"Based on the third-quarter results we maintain our forecast that 1996 will be a good year for DSM," the statement quoted DSM chairman Simon de Bree as saying.
De Bree said that investments of 1.3 billion guilders over 1996 to date were targeted mainly at strengthening DSM's fine chemical activities.
